title: Nominet DRS D00028947 (cashconversions.co.uk) — Cash Converters Pty Limited v Cash Conversions
text:
Dispute Resolution Service
DRS 28947
Decision of an Independent Expert
Cash Converters Pty Limited
and
Cash Conversions
1. Parties
Complainant: Cash Converters Pty Limited
84 Theobalds Road
Lacon
London
WC1X 8NL
United Kingdom
Respondent: Cash Conversions
303 Harehills Lane
Leeds
West Yorkshire
LS9 6AA
United Kingdom
2. Domain Name
cashconversions.co.uk (the “Domain Name”)
1

3. Procedural Background
On 26th March 2026, the Complaint was lodged with Nominet UK Limited (“Nominet”) and it was
validated on 27th March 2026. On 27th March 2026, Nominet sent the notification of the Complaint
letter to the Respondent by e-mail and post, advising the Respondent to log into Nominet’s online
services to view the details of the Complaint, and giving the Respondent 15 business days within
which to lodge a Response on or before 21st April 2026. On 17th April 2026, Nominet sent the
Respondent a Response reminder. On 21st April 2026, the Respondent sent a Response. On 21st April
2026, Nominet advised the Complainant that a Response had been received and advised it to log
into Nominet’s Online Services to view it. Nominet invited the Complainant to make a Reply on or
before 28th April 2026. On 24th April 2026, Nominet sent the Complainant a Reply reminder. On 28th
April 2026, the Complainant sent a Reply. On 28th April 2026, Nominet advised the Respondent a
Reply had been received. Mediation documents were generated for the Complaint, and mediation
commenced on 1st May 2026. Mediation was unsuccessful and concluded on 1st May 2026, and on
1st May 2026 Nominet sent close of mediation documents. On 11th May 2026, the Complainant paid
the appropriate fee for a Decision to be made by an Expert pursuant to paragraph 6 of Nominet’s
DRS Policy (“the Policy”).
On 12th May 2026, Mr Niall Lawless (“the Expert”) was notified of his appointment to act as Expert
in this dispute and is required to give his Decision by 8th June 2026. The Expert has confirmed that
he is independent of each of the Parties and that, to the best of his knowledge and belief, there are
no facts or circumstances, past or present, or that could arise in the foreseeable future, that need
to be disclosed as they might be of such a nature as to call into question his independence in the
eyes of one or both of the Parties.
On 14th May 2026, Nominet sent the Parties an “Expert Request for Further Information”: “The
Expert notes that whereas the Complaint refers to Annex 1 to 7, the Annexes document available via
Nominet online services appears to consist only of one cover page “Annex 1”. Pursuant to paragraph
17.1 of the Policy, the Expert offers the Complainant the opportunity to submit Annex 1 to 7 before
the end of Wednesday 20th May 2026. Should the Respondent wish to make any submissions in
respect of Annex 1 to 7, it should do so before the end of Wednesday, 27th May 2026.”
On 18th May 2026, the Complainant submitted the Complaint Annex 1 to 7. The Respondent made
no submissions in respect of Annex 1 to 7.
2

4. Outstanding Formal or Procedural Issues
There are no outstanding formal or procedural issues.
5. Factual Background
The Complainant, Cash Converters Pty Limited and its subsidiary Cash Converters (UK) Limited
(individually or together "Cash Converters") was formed in 1984 and first opened its CASH
CONVERTERS branded business in the UK in 1991. It is a global retail and financial services company
that specialises in buying and selling second-hand goods and providing financial services, including
lines of credit.
The Respondent, Cash Conversions, serving the local community in Leeds, UK, since 2011, specialises
in buying gold, electronics, and other items of value, providing instant cash with no hidden fees or
hassle.
The Respondent registered the Domain Name on 7th July 2011, and it resolves to a website
promoting its products and services.
6. The Parties’ Contentions
The Complainant
The Complainant says that it has rights in a name that is identical to the Domain Name, and it seeks
transfer of the Domain Name.
In summary, the Complainant says that the Domain Name in the hands of the Respondent is abusive
because:
• The Domain Name is being used in a way is likely to confuse people or businesses into believing
that the Domain Name is registered to, operated or authorised by, or otherwise connected with
the Complainant.
• The Domain Name resolves to a website where the content offered is identical and/or similar
services to that of the Complainant.
• The Domain Name resolves to a website that shares a colour scheme and format with that of the
Complainant.
• Any misrepresentation of an affiliation or association with the Complainant is likely to disrupt its
business by way of consumer confusion, which may tarnish the reputation of the Complainant
and/or result in a loss of sales.
3

• The Respondent’s use of the Domain Name takes “unfair advantage” because the Respondent
has benefitted from the Complainant’s repute without expending any effort of its own.
• The Respondent has not provided any evidence to support its position.
• There is no connection or co-operation between the Complainant and the Respondent.
The Respondent
In summary, the Respondent says that the Domain Name is not an Abusive Registration because:
• It has traded under the name “Cash Conversions” for a long period of time.
• It is an independent business and has never claimed to be the Complainant.
• It has not created a misleading imitation website.
• The Domain Name matches its genuine trading name.
• The Domain Name was registered for legitimate business use.
• The Domain Name has been used in connection with genuine business activity.
• The Domain Name was not registered for sale, disruption, deception, or unfair gain.
• There has been no unfair advantage taken of the Complainant’s rights.
• There has been no unfair detriment caused to the Complainant.
• The Complaint does not establish abusive registration as required by the Policy.
7. Discussion and Findings
7.1 General
The Policy requires that for a Complaint to succeed, the Complainant must prove to the Expert on the
balance of probabilities that:
i. the Complainant has Rights in respect of a name or mark which is identical or similar to the
Domain Name; and
ii. the Domain Name, in the hands of the Respondent, is an Abusive Registration.
Rights include, but are not limited to, rights enforceable under English law.
7.2 The Complainant’s Rights
The Complainant’s name is Cash Converters Pty Limited, and its UK subsidiary is Cash Converters (UK)
Limited. The Complainant has provided evidence that it is the proprietor of a number of registered
trademarks for CASH CONVERTERS including UK Trademark numbers UK00001463232 registered on
1st October 1993 and UK00002588064 registered on 25th November 2011; and European Union
4

trademark number 001810498 registered on 10th October 2003 and the comparable United Kingdom
trademark No. UK00901810498 created following the United Kingdom’s exit from the European
Union, and also treated as registered on 10th October 2003; In the UK the Complainant conducts
business at <www.cashconverters.co.uk>.
The Domain Name is similar to the Complainant’s name and the ‘CASH CONVERTERS” trademark and
the Complainant’s UK trading domain name.
Accordingly, based on the evaluation of the evidence presented, the Expert decides that the
Complainant has Rights in respect of a name or mark that is identical or similar to the Domain Name.
7.3 Abusive Registration
The Complainant says that the Domain Name controlled by the Respondent is an Abusive Registration
under the Policy. Under paragraph 5 “Evidence of Abusive Registration”, guidance is given as to what
factors may be evidence that the Domain Name is an Abusive Registration.
“A non-exhaustive list of factors which may be evidence that the Domain Name is an Abusive
Registration is as follows:
5.1.1 Circumstances indicating that the Respondent has registered or otherwise acquired the Domain
Name primarily:
5.1.1.1 for the purposes of selling, renting or otherwise transferring the Domain Name to the
Complainant or to a competitor of the Complainant, for valuable consideration in excess of the
Respondent's documented out-of-pocket costs directly associated with acquiring or using the
Domain Name;
5.1.1.2 as a blocking registration against a name or mark in which the Complainant has Rights; or
5.1.1.3 for the purpose of unfairly disrupting the business of the Complainant;
5.1.2 Circumstances indicating that the Respondent is using or threatening to use the Domain Name
in a way which has confused or is likely to confuse people or businesses into believing that the Domain
Name is registered to, operated or authorised by, or otherwise connected with the Complainant.”
5

Confusion and unfair advantage
The Complainant
As set out above, the Complainant says that the Domain Name is being used in a way is likely to
confuse people or businesses into believing that the Domain Name is registered to, operated or
authorised by, or otherwise connected with the Complainant.
To support this contention, the Complainant says that the Domain Name resolves to a website where
the content is identical and/or similar services to that of the Complainant, and that the website shares
the same colour scheme and format as that of the Complainant.
The Complainant says that, on the balance of probabilities, the Respondent has, from the time it
registered the Domain Name on 7th July 2011, taken unfair advantage benefitting from the repute of
the Complainant’s Cash Converters marks without expending any effort of its own. The Complainant
supports this contention by referring the Expert to Cash Converters Pty Limited and Cash Converters
(UK) Limited) Annual Report 2011, which records that the Cash Converters UK online store generated
39,043,271 page views, from 2,144,386 unique visitors.
The Respondent
The Respondent says that similarity between the names “Cash Conversions” and “Cash Converters” is
not enough to cause confusion.
The Responding Party says that its longstanding use of the name “Cash Conversions” demonstrates
that it is commonly known by that name and it has built goodwill in it through its own efforts. The
Responding Party says that over time, it has invested money, work, and reputation into promoting its
business identity. The Responding Party says the Domain Name supports that legitimate trading
presence.
Expert’s Reasoning and Decision
The Expert accepts the Complainant’s assertion that there is no connection between the Complainant
and the Respondent.
The Complainant is correct that the Respondent has not provided any evidence to support its
contentions. In the Response, the Respondent merely stated: “We reserve the right to provide further
supporting evidence if required.”
6

Confusion would arise where the internet user incorrectly assumes that the website the Domain
Names resolves to is authorised by or belongs to the Complainant.
Despite the Domain Name being registered on 7th July 2011, the Complainant has not provided any
actual evidence of confusion.
The Complainant and the Respondent are each entitled to operate in the same business space and
offer identical and/or similar services, and it is completely normal that there would be some overlap
in content and format.
However, after undertaking a review of the Complainant’s website <www.cashconverters.co.uk> and
the Respondents website <www.cashconversions.co.uk>, the Expert decides that the websites are not
similar and it is unlikely that a visitor would be confused that both websites are operated by the
Complainant.
Accordingly, the Respondents use of the Domain Name does not take “unfair advantage” of the
Complainants repute.
Under the Policy, one of the factors which may be evidence that the Domain Name is not an Abusive
Registration is that before being aware of the Complainant’s cause for complaint (not necessarily the
‘complaint’ under the DRS), the Respondent has used or made demonstrable preparations to use the
Domain Name or a domain name which is similar to the Domain Name in connection with a genuine
offering of goods or services.
The Respondent registered the Domain Name on 7th July 2011, and it resolves to a website promoting
its products and services.
The Expert notes that the “Wayback Machine” offering an Internet Archive, records the Domain Name
being used for a website as far back as 8th April 2013.
In addition to this, the website the Domain Name resolves to refers the visitor to dedicated stores
where they can have their items valued, swap foreign currency, or explore their pre-owned retail
selection. Google Maps identifies the addresses located as: “Cash Conversions Pawn shop”. The
physical premises are:
7

• Cash Conversions (Harehills): Located at 303 Harehills Lane, LS9 6AA.
• Cash Converters (Kirkgate): Located at 19 Kirkgate, LS1 6BY.
• Cash Converters (York Road): Located at 459 York Road, LS9 6TA.
• Cash Converters (Beeston): Located on Dewsbury Road.
The Expert has no hesitation in deciding that the Respondent is a legitimate business using the Domain
Name in connection with a genuine offering of goods or services.
The Respondent has offered persuasive reasons why the Domain Name is not an Abusive Registration
considering the factors as set out in paragraph 8 of the Policy.
Accordingly, the Expert concludes that under the test as set out in paragraph 5.1.2 of the Policy, in
the hands of the Respondent the Domain Name is not an Abusive Registration.
7.4 Conclusion
The Expert finds on the balance of probabilities that the Complainant has Rights in respect of a name
or mark identical or similar to the Domain Name but that the Complainant has not proved, on the
balance of probabilities, that the Domain Name in the hands of the Respondent is an Abusive
Registration.
8. Decision
For the reasons set out in detail above, the Expert directs that the Domain Name registration will
therefore remain with the Respondent.
Niall Lawless, Nominet Expert
1st June 2026
8
